description: Manuscript set B (n = 1, w = 4) (decaying signal, leaky abortion b_R = 0.5), sweeping the priming reversion rate rho. Stop-and-go needs a finite primed patch (gamma_s > 0) that reverts on a timescale separated from the run phase (conditions C1-C6, § 3.11). Uses the manuscript density cutoff (no infection below V_ext = p_ext, removal at rate 5); without it, stalls restart by non-physical tail tunnelling.

expected.rho <~ 0.003 (near-permanent priming): stall: the front arrests (a front with no strategy is dead, § 6.4); checked at rho = 0.001
expected.rho >~ 0.01: stop_and_go: periodic stalls and restarts; checked T_cycle ~ 20 at rho = 0.03 and ~ 11 at rho = 1
expected.rho -> large: still stop_and_go: the stall cannot be shorter than the signal-decay time Lambda / gamma_s ~ 7 (eq. 54), so reversion alone does not produce a smooth wave here; see the set A sweeps for steady waves
